messages:
ben: Heads up — the canary for r128 (merge a1b2c3d) is showing a p95 latency spike on the 'decoder-XL' profile, ~+18% vs baseline. Noticed right after kernel-selector changes landed.
perf-bot: CI perf check failed for a1b2c3d: p95 +18%, throughput -12% on decoder workloads. See /dash/perf/1789.
priya: Ugh. Was the batching heuristic tweak included in that merge too? I remember a change to max_batch_age.
marco: Yes — PR #3421 touched kernel selection and the dynamic batch shaping in the same patch. The git diff shows kernel_selector.py and batch_controller changes.
cara: Quick log snippet from the canary host: ```
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] kernel_picker: fallback to generic_kernel
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] kv_cache: miss_rate increase from 0.12 -> 0.46
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] batcher: flush due to max_age
```
ben: That fallback to generic_kernel is suspicious — we should see that under rare model shapes, but not this frequently. Looks like kernel selection decided the optimized kernels weren't compatible with the new batching alignment.
jae: I ran a perf profile on the canary instance with flamegraphs attached. Main hotspot is memcpy + kernel_dispatch overhead when batch shapes oscillate. Attaching snippet: ```
hotspots:
  memcpy: 34.2%
  kernel_dispatch: 28.7%
  kv_lookup: 12.1%
  scheduler_spin: 8.3%
```
priya: KV cache miss spike explains extra memcpy/dispatch — more activations reloaded. Could be the batcher causing more unique prefixes per batch which invalidates prefix/KV reuse.
perf-bot: Bisect suggestion: suspect range a1b2c3d..f4e5d6c — most likely culprit PR: #3421. Automated bisect yields test failure reproduction on commit a1b2c3d.
marco: I started a manual bisect across kernel_selector and batch_controller commits — locally reproduces when both changes are present. If I roll back just kernel_selector, perf looks normal. If I roll back only batch_controller, still bad but less severe. So combination amplifies.
alice: So it's an interaction: kernel selection + batch shaping leads to worse KV cache locality and more generic kernel fallbacks.
ben: Canary is currently at 4% traffic. deploy-bot: Canary deployment r128 started at 1761234567, current weight 4%. No automatic rollback triggered.
cara: Why didn't auto-rollback fire? Our gate is p95 +15% OR error_rate > 2%. We hit +18% p95 — should have rolled back.
je: There was a mis-config in the deployment policy for this release: canary_gates were disabled for the region due to a previous test. Ops ticket opened: #OPS-907.
priya: Ok, immediate plan: 1) pause rollout and pin traffic back to 0 for r128; 2) revert kernel_selector change from a1b2c3d; 3) add an integration perf check that simulates decoder-XL batching shapes; 4) fix canary gate config so auto-rollback can't be globally disabled.
ben: I paused the rollout and set canary weight to 0 manually. Confirmed.
perf-bot: Action recorded: manual_pause by ben at 1761234582. Canary weight -> 0.
marco: I'll prepare a revert PR limited to kernel_selector and run the full perf benchmarks in CI before we re-run canary.
jae: Also adding a microbenchmark that exercises alternating short/long sequences to catch KV churn. We should fail CI if p95 regresses >10% on that benchmark.
cara: We should also add a guard in runtime: if kernel_selector falls back to generic more than X% in a minute, emit a metric and trigger immediate canary pause. That would catch this behavior even if canary gates get misconfigured.
alice: Good idea. We can implement a sliding window fallback_rate metric and tie it to deploy-bot.
je: Short-term: revert kernel_selector in prod canary. Medium: fix batch shaping to preserve prefix grouping heuristics and adjust cache TTL/eviction to be a bit more conservative when batch composition churns.
priya: I've filed follow-ups: INF-1289 (revert kernel_selector), INF-1290 (batcher conservative mode), INF-1291 (canary gate hardening). Assigning Marco INF-1289, Jae INF-1290, Cara INF-1291.
marco: Working on INF-1289, will cut revert PR in next 30m and run perf CI.
ben: Postmortem note: don't land cross-cutting perf-sensitive changes (kernel + batching) in same PR. If unavoidable, require perf CI that mirrors canary traffic shapes.
perf-bot: CI run for revert PR started. Baseline checks will take ~18 minutes.
priya: Thanks everyone. Let's keep updates here. If revert doesn't fix it, we'll bisect deeper into quantized-kernel selection path.
ben: TL;DR: canary flagged p95 +18% due to interaction between kernel selector and batching heuristics causing KV cache churn and kernel fallbacks. Canary didn't auto-rollback due to config leak; rollout paused and revert in flight.
cara: Adding a quick dashboard tile to show kernel_fallback_rate and kv_miss_rate per canary in future canary cards.
marco: Revert PR: https://git.redwood/a/PR/3490 (in progress).
ben: I'll close the loop once CI + canary prove revert safe. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
